text: The OECD AI Principles are a set of non-binding principles adopted by the OECD Council in May 2019 and updated in 2024. This initiative within the OECD intergovernmental organization sets out a voluntary framework for trustworthy AI. Lead: OECD secretariat. Scope: global, 47 adhering countries.

The AI Safety Summit held at Bletchley Park in November 2023 was hosted by the UK government with 28 countries attending. It produced the Bletchley Declaration on frontier AI safety risks. This one-off summit was state-to-state, global in scope, and its non-binding declaration on AI safety has been influential.

ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42 is a standards body working group established in October 2017 as a subcommittee of ISO. It develops technical standards for AI interoperability including ISO/IEC 22989 (terminology) and 23894 (risk management). Lead actor: igo secretariat (ISO). Scope: global. Outputs are voluntary standards with soft-law character. Topic focus: interoperability of AI systems.

The Frontier Model Forum is an industry-led consortium founded in July 2023 by Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI. It provides dialogue and coordination on frontier AI safety practices across its corporate members. Lead actor: industry. Scope: global. Outputs are non-binding industry commitments (soft-law).

The Council of Europe Ad hoc Committee on AI (CAHAI) operated 2019-2022 under the Council of Europe as a research and study body. Its mandate was to conduct a feasibility study and produce research on AI ethics and human rights. Regional scope: Council of Europe (European region). Lead actor: Council of Europe secretariat. Legal character: mixed outputs (soft-law interim study heading toward a future instrument).

EAAMO (Equity and Access in Algorithms, Mechanisms, and Optimization) is a standalone annual academic conference first held in 2021, ACM-hosted with peer-reviewed research proceedings. Topic focus: equity and access in algorithmic systems. Lead actor: academia. Scope: global. Legal character: n/a (academic conference, no normative output).

The UK AI Security Institute (formerly AI Safety Institute) is the UK's national frontier AI safety body, founded November 2023. Its primary work is capability evaluation and red-teaming of frontier models. Lead: AISI under UK state government (DSIT). Scope: global coordination via the International AISI Network. Outputs: mixed — voluntary evaluations plus guidance.

The European AI Office is a regulatory enforcement body established under EU Regulation 2024/1689 (the AI Act). It supervises general-purpose AI models and enforces the AI Act across the European Union. Scope: regional (EU). Lead: state government level enforcement. Legal character: hard-law.

The G7 Hiroshima AI Process is an intergovernmental forum among G7 states producing the G7 Hiroshima Code of Conduct for organisations developing advanced frontier AI. Scope: plurilateral (G7). Lead: state-to-state cooperation. Legal character: non-binding soft-law outputs.

The Future of Life Institute is an international non-profit civil-society think tank founded in 2014, focused on research and monitoring of frontier AI safety risks. Scope: global. Legal character: n/a (research-only, no normative output).
